evidence.text: The Introduction to Software Engineering course provides students with fundamental knowledge of software engineering, including methods, principles, techniques, tools, and key activities in industrial software projects, as well as modern software development trends, particularly the application of artificial intelligence in software engineering. This helps students develop systematic thinking, process-oriented working methods, and a foundation for advanced courses in the field of software engineering.
Explain the role, scope, and significance of software engineering in information system development;

Explain and describe the basic concepts of software engineering, including methods, principles, techniques, and tools, and identify modern software development trends, particularly automation, artificial intelligence, and digital transformation in software engineering;
Explain the role of key activities in industrial software projects, such as requirements analysis, design, programming, testing, software project management, and software quality assurance.
Apply fundamental knowledge of software engineering to analyze simple practical scenarios and problems;
Develop analytical skills and clarify the role of each activity in the software development process;
Cultivate skills and enhance the ability to use methods, tools, documentation, techniques, and international guidelines/models to ensure software products meet user objectives.
Select and apply a suitable process model for a software project that meets user objectives. Establish processes in software development projects according to the chosen model.

Explain and describe the basic concepts of software engineering in information system development; methods, principles, techniques, tools, models, and international standards in the field of software, modern software development trends and digital transformation in software engineering; the role of key activities in software projects according to industrial processes; as well as analyze requirements and propose software solutions to meet user objectives in practical problems.
Select and apply methods, tools, and techniques to control software products to meet user objectives.

Compile and effectively present key documents in practical software development projects, including: business requirement documents; software requirement specification documents; system design documents; user manuals; and team project reports.
